# Best portable power stations for camping

For most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the sweet spot. It covers phones, lights, camera batteries, and a CPAP, and it's light enough to carry one-handed. Go bigger only if you want to run a fridge or cooler for several days.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 288Wh)

- **Bluetti Elite 30 V2** (288Wh, 600W, 4.3 kg): $289.99, or $275.50 with code AFF5OFF. TechRadar names it its budget pick. [Buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2). One caveat: Dealectric says its solar input tops out at 28V, so many 100W+ folding panels won't work. TechRadar lists 200W solar input, so check the panel compatibility before buying.
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (288Wh, 300W, 8.3 lb): about $249. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) ranks it best overall for camping. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so the Plus is only sold through Amazon and other retailers. That site gave no direct product link, so search for it by name.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (288Wh, 300W, 5-year warranty): about $199, with a built-in lantern, per the same guide. Make sure you buy the version with an AC outlet, not the "C300 DC."
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (286Wh, 600W, expandable to 572Wh): about $269-299, also per that guide.

Be aware that OutdoorGearLab's lab testing scored the Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low against bigger units. These small models are fine for phones and lights, but they aren't strong performers.

## Longer trips or running a fridge (1,000Wh+)

- **Bluetti AC180** (1,152Wh, 1,800W, about 35 lb): $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF. [Buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). It has no expansion port.
- **ALLPOWERS P1800** (1,024Wh, 1,800W): $395.10 with code ALLPOWERS26. [Buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh). Its warranty is only 24 months.
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** (2,042Wh, 39 lb): [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) picked it as best for off-grid camping, and it's now under $900 on Amazon. It's heavy, and it can't run a space heater or electric burner for long.
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's best value, on sale for under $530. It's compact but has a noisy fan.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**: TechRadar's camping pick, with easy solar charging. See [TechRadar's list](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations).

## My pick

For a typical weekend, I'd get the **Bluetti Elite 30 V2**. It's the lightest, cheapest, and best-reviewed small option that has a direct buy link. If you want a fridge or multi-day power, the **Bluetti AC180** is the best-priced option I found.

## Caveats

- The Dealectric links are affiliate links, and Dealectric only covers Bluetti, ALLPOWERS, and Tenergy. It can't compare against Jackery, EcoFlow, or Anker.
- PowerStationGearLab also earns affiliate commissions, and its star ratings aren't backed by the kind of lab numbers OutdoorGearLab publishes.
- Prices change often, and Black Friday is close, so check the current price before buying.
- Turn off your CPAP's humidifier, which can triple its power draw.

Tell me what you plan to run (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and how many nights, and I can narrow this to one pick.
